## lib-google-calendar — CONTRACT (EA calendar slice)
THE credential-holding Google Calendar access point for the EA slice. It runs on the shared full-scope **`Google Calendar account`** credential (operator decision — one credential, not a second read-only one).

**WRITES EXIST HERE (create/update/delete) AND ARE NOT UNGATED.** The only caller is `cc-calendar-facade`, whose only caller is Central Command's Executor, which runs a capability only after the operator approved the proposal naming it. Agents hold `propose_calendar_change` and nothing else; `runtime/` cannot even import the tier that calls this. What must never be added here is a mode that some *other* client could drive, or a second webhook onto this lib.

**INPUT** (single item, from `cc-calendar-facade`):
- `{ mode:'list', time_min, time_max, calendar_id?, max_results? }` → `{ ok:true, events:[…], truncated }`
  Each event: `{ start, end, all_day, summary, location, attendee_count, organizer_is_self, has_agenda, declined }`
- `{ mode:'create_event', title, start, end, description?, attendees?, calendar_id? }` → `{ ok:true, event:{ event_id, html_link, summary, start, end } }`
- `{ mode:'update_event', event_id, calendar_id?, …any of title|start|end|description|attendees }` → same event shape. **PATCH**: only the keys present change. At least one must be present.
- `{ mode:'delete_event', event_id, calendar_id? }` → `{ ok:true, deleted:event_id }`. A 410 (already gone) is success — the desired state holds.

`start`/`end`/`time_*` are RFC3339 with an explicit offset or `Z`, sent as `{dateTime}` with **no `timeZone` key** (a second source of truth for the instant is how a meeting lands an hour off). `calendar_id` defaults to `primary`. All three writes carry **`sendUpdates=all`** — change it in all three URLs together, and say so here.

**FAILURES**: one `fail()` helper per Return node. n8n splits a Code-node error message on the LAST `': '` and surfaces only the tail — so `fail()` neutralises every colon in the body and raw provider text goes to `console.log` only, never into a thrown message (a leak class an earlier provider workflow had).

### ✅ NO MANUAL STEPS
The credential is already bound on all four provider nodes: **Google Calendar account**
(`googleCalendarOAuth2Api`, resolved by NAME at import). Nothing on this canvas needs editing.

What bounds this lib is the mode allowlist in **Validate request** plus the fact
that its only caller is `cc-calendar-facade` (→ Central Command's Executor, post-approval),
not the credential's scopes.

**Why raw `httpRequest` and not the `googleCalendar` node:** that node's
Calendar field validates the id against an EMAIL regex, so the literal
`primary` can never be addressed through it. It also surfaces no HTTP
status, which left the 401/403/404/410/429 classification in the Return nodes
unreachable. `fullResponse` + `neverError` + `onError:continueRegularOutput` are
what make that classification possible — do not simplify them away.
